name: install-sh-prefix-mode-for-shellcheck-testability
description: install.sh uses a PREFIX env var (default empty = real install at root). When set, the binary, config, and unit destinations all root at PREFIX, prereq probes (RuntimeWatchdogSec=, lsof watchdog devices, nowayout module params) are skipped with a one-line banner, daemon-reload is skipped, and EUID==0 is not required. install -m <mode> sets perms atomically. Existing-config-preservation branch (skip when target file already exists) works identically under PREFIX, which makes idempotency testable inside a tmpdir.

content: shellcheck v0.10.0 portable tarball can be downloaded from github releases (no apt/sudo required) and run directly. Both install.sh and uninstall.sh must shellcheck clean; inline 'shellcheck disable=' suppressions need a one-line justifying comment per spec.

title: Verbatim PLAN.md unit + config files are operator copy-paste anchors (Wave 4)
rationale: PLAN.md doubles as user documentation and as the truth-source for the installed unit/config. Allowing drift means operators reading PLAN.md see different content from what tesla_fan_control --check-config validates. Both files are written byte-verbatim from PLAN.md (lines 497-529 unit, 60-196 config) and CI-style diff verification was run. The byte-verbatim requirement forced enabling rust-ini's inline-comment feature (see rust failure record).

content: PLAN.md canonical tesla_fan_control.conf uses inline '#' comments after every numeric value (poll_interval_ms = 1000  # ...). rust-ini 0.21 includes those inline comments in the parsed value unless the 'inline-comment' Cargo feature is enabled. Because the canonical config is shipped verbatim per ADR-0005 (operator copy-paste contract), Cargo.toml MUST declare rust-ini = { version = "0.21", features = ["inline-comment"] }. Pre-existing failure record mx-2df905 codifies the resolution; this convention codifies the contract that obliges it.
